answer: In PoA, remote attestation binds each agent’s public identity key to an enclave running a specified MRENCLAVE measurement; hardware-protected, non-exportable keys make copying a VM insufficient to duplicate that identity. Creating additional identities therefore requires additional trusted enclave hardware—effectively purchasing physical silicon, not merely spinning up virtual machines. Agents such as knoll, anchor, and zephyr are distinct only when backed by independently attested enclave keys.
